description: Danielle Pletka, American Enterprise Institute Distinguished Fellow, discusses the latest with the Trump Administration and Iran & how she thinks President Trump might use the naval carrier strike group that is headed toward the Mediterranean. She also talks about the reactions from Canada & the UK following President Trump's remarks in Davos. Danielle speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pletka on Trump, Iran, & World Leaders Reaction to Trump

description: Craig Fugate, former FEMA Administrator under the Obama Administration, shares what he expects to happen this weekend regarding the massive winter storm set to effect a large portion of the US. He voices his concerns over large ice accumulations that will cause power outages, if FEMA is ready, and his thoughts on FEMA halting terminations due to this storm. Craig speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Does FEMA Expect From Winter Storm?

description: Apple plans to revamp Siri later this year by turning the digital assistant into the company’s first artificial intelligence chatbot, thrusting the iPhone maker into a generative AI race dominated by OpenAI and Google. The chatbot — code-named Campos — will be embedded deeply into the iPhone, iPad and Mac operating systems and replace the current Siri interface, according to people familiar with the plan. Users will be able to summon the new service the same way they open Siri now, by speaking the “Siri” command or holding down the side button on their iPhone or iPad. Meanwhile, Apple has expanded the job of hardware chief John Ternus to include design work, solidifying his status as a leading contender to eventually succeed Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook. Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Global Consumer Tech Mark Gurman joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Apple to Revamp Siri as Built-In Chatbot; Hardware Chief Becomes CEO Contender

description:
TikTok and its Chinese parent ByteDance Ltd. have closed a long-awaited deal to transfer parts of their US operations to American investors, securing the popular video app’s future in the US and avoiding a nationwide ban. The social media company has officially established a US entity with three managing investors: Oracle, private equity firm Silver Lake Management LLC and Abu Dhabi-based investment company MGX. TikTok Chief Executive Officer Shou Chew — who will continue running ByteDance’s most valuable asset globally — gets a seat on the board. Adam Presser, who was TikTok’s head of operations, trust and safety, will now helm the American venture as CEO.
Bloomberg News Technology Reporter Alexandra Levine joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. She speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: TikTok Seals Deal to Operate in the US After Years of Drama

description: Snow and dangerously bitter cold are spreading from the Rocky Mountains to the Great Lakes as a massive storm pushes toward the US Northeast, disrupting travel and threatening power outages for much of the nation. The storm is expected to span nearly 1,500 miles (2,400 kilometers), bringing heavy snow, crippling ice and subzero wind chill to some of the biggest US cities. Natural gas prices surged on concern iced-over equipment will choke supplies. Airlines have already canceled almost 4,000 flights and Amtrak has pulled dozens of trips from its schedule. Bloomberg News Energy Reporter Josh Saul joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Massive Storm to Test Power Grids Across US This Weekend

author: Mark Niquette
description: Some economists question whether robust consumption can be sustained.
title: Americans Are Spending Faster Than Their Incomes Are Rising

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss a major winter storm set to sweep across the US across the weekend and the impact it could have on power grids, especially in the south. Bloomberg's Josh Saul joins the show with more details. Then, Wayne Sanders of Bloomberg Intelligence weighs in on President Trump's push to remove limits on the US military in Greenland, and Andrew Krei of Crescent Grove Advisors discusses how markets are ingesting geopolitical tensions and the rotation trade. Plus, Bloomberg's Alexandra Levine on the finalizing of a US TikTok entity, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman on his exclusive reporting about Apple's Siri revamp. Finally, Morgan Stanley's Lauren Hochfelder on the real estate outlook for 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Major Storm Set to Sweep US, S&P Sees Two-Week Loss | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 1/23/2026

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the upcoming snowstorm. On today's show, former FEMA Administrator Deanne Criswell, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Republican Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Readies for Massive Winter Storm | Balance of Power: Early Edition 1/23/2026

author: Kelcee Griffis
description: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr sees “legitimate competition concerns” in Netflix Inc.’s proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc.’s studios and streaming businesses, concerns he doesn’t share if Paramount Skydance Corp. were to acquire those assets.
title: FCC Chief Sees ‘Competition Concerns’ in Netflix-Warner Deal

description: New York Representative Nicole Malliotakis, the only Republican to represent the city in Washington, says that the goal of recent efforts to change the boundaries of her district is to ensure Democrat wins. Malliotakis also weighed in on the city's preparation for winter weather, saying the storm is a test for Mayor Zohran Mamdani and he'll get the heat if roads are cleared properly.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: NYC Redistricting Goal to Ensure 'Republican Can Never Win,' Says Malliotakis

description: Former FEMA Administrator Deanne Criswell said the agency is facing the coming winter storm short of staff, and that will make it harder to keep up with the requests for help from state and local officials. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: FEMA Staff Cuts Strains Ability to Help Communities, Says Former Administrator

description: Congress is getting closer to fully funding the government. The House passed its final six spending bills—more than $1.2 trillion—sending the package to the Senate ahead of the January 30 deadline. The deal locks in fiscal 2026 funding and adds guardrails against Trump administration funding shifts. Senate action is expected next week. Representative Jason Smith, the House Ways and Means Chairman--the top tax official in Congress--joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about what comes next and how his committee is trying to tackle the rising cost of US health care. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Funding Deal Heads to the Senate

author: Nancy Cook, Joshua Green, Saleha Mohsin
description: Rick Rieder’s Wall Street bona fides and openness to making changes at the Federal Reserve have bolstered his candidacy for the central bank’s top job, according to people familiar with the White House deliberations.
title: Rieder’s Market Support, Fed Plans Seen as Boon for Chair Job

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, President Trump says the US can 'do anything we want' in the Greenland framework deal, including actions related to the military. 

Russian President Vladimir Putin held about four hours of talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in the Kremlin on the latest peace plan aimed at ending his war on Ukraine. 

Gold closed in on $5,000 an ounce, with geopolitical risks and renewed threats to the Federal Reserve’s independence supporting a record-breaking rally.

Today's guests: Lale Akoner, Global Market Analyst at eToro, Denmark Opposition MP Sascha Faxe and Ericsson CEO Börje Ekholm. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Greenland Framework Lets US do Whatever it Wants | Daybreak Europe 1/23/2026
